Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of findings: Minutes after a bee/wasp sting to the arm, patient reports mild dyspnea and a sensation of right-sided lip swelling and “weird” tongue. Video exam shows normal breathing and speech, no visible lip/oropharyngeal swelling, and a localized puncture with mild erythema on the arm without notable swelling. Past history includes eczema and occasional anxiety/panic; penicillin allergy.  
- Working diagnosis: Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to Hymenoptera sting.  
- Supporting DDx rationale: Consistent with immediate localized erythema and puncture mark, absence of objective airway involvement, and stable clinical appearance.  
- Considerations (from DDx, plausible but uncertain):  
  - Early anaphylaxis (IgE-mediated) — medium likelihood given temporal association and subjective dyspnea/oral sensations, but no objective findings or progression observed.  
  - Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea — medium likelihood due to history of panic and normal observed respirations.  
  - Histaminergic angioedema of lips/tongue — low likelihood without visible swelling or progression.  
  - Early cellulitis — low likelihood shortly after sting without warmth or spreading erythema.  
- Plan:  
  - Start antihistamine: chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg up to six times daily or a once-daily non-sedating antihistamine (specific product/dose not documented).  
  - Safety-netting: Seek urgent care/ED immediately if lip/tongue swelling develops, breathing difficulty, stridor, voice change, generalized hives, dizziness/syncope, or rapidly worsening symptoms.  
  - Monitor local site; if redness spreads, becomes hot/tender, or systemic signs develop, reassess for possible antibiotic therapy (penicillin allergy noted).  
  - No immediate need for allergy testing; consider if recurrent reactions or atypical rashes occur.  
  - Follow-up with clinic if symptoms persist, worsen, or for reassurance.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to Hymenoptera sting — High likelihood: Immediate localized erythema with puncture mark and no objective airway involvement.  
- Early anaphylaxis (IgE-mediated) — Medium likelihood: Temporal link with subjective dyspnea/oral sensations but no visible swelling, wheeze/stridor, or progression.  
- Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea — Medium likelihood: History of panic with normal observed breathing and speech suggests psychogenic component.
